intro: You are about to enter Trabzon Museum, in Trabzon province, opened in 2001. The building is the Kostaki mansion: its painted ceilings and joinery have been left in place, and on the floor below wait the region's Roman and Byzantine finds.
history: The house was built between the end of the nineteenth century and the start of the twentieth for the banker Kostaki Theophylaktos. It later passed to the Nemlizade family, and in 1924 it served as Atatürk's residence in the city. Once restored, it opened as a museum in 2001, with its painted ceilings and joinery left in place and the region's Roman and Byzantine finds on the floor below.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rooms of the Kostaki mansion and their painted ceilings; then visit the Roman and Byzantine finds, and save time for the ethnography floor.
facts: Did you know? Here the rooms are as much on show as the collection: the painted decoration of their ceilings is among the best preserved of Black Sea mansion work from the turn of the twentieth century. And this banking family's mansion became, in 1924, Atatürk's residence in Trabzon.
outro: This brings our tour of Trabzon Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these rooms stay as beautiful for the next visitor. Thank you, and enjoy your visit.
